paras: The beating of Joseph White took place on August 11, 1903, near Newport, Delaware, when armed men pursued White, a Black man accused of robbing a family that had sheltered him, caught him in the woods, beat him and let him go. The Wilmington Evening Journal, the only paper found to report it, identified him as a cousin of George White, described as lynched for the murder of Helen Bishop.

According to the Evening Journal's Newport correspondent, White spent the night of August 10 at State Road with a family who did not know him but took him in and fed him. The next morning the head of the family found White gone and said that $20, a gold watch, a revolver and a music box had gone with him.

The householder roused his neighbors and followed a report that a man matching White's description was heading toward Newport. In Newport the town was "thrown into a state of excitement" as White was seen being chased by three men "flourishing pistols and guns." Traced to a house in "colored row," White jumped the back fence and ran across Robert Lynam's field and the Snyder farm into the woods.

There, near the spot the paper associated with George White's crime, the pursuers captured him after a brief struggle. They recovered the money, watch and revolver, but not the music box he had thrown away, then gave him "a heavy thrashing" and released him.
The report mentions no officers, arrest or charge against either White or the men who beat him, and no follow-up report was found.

The Evening Journal ran the story on page 6 on August 12 under the headline "Robbed People Who Took Him In," presenting the robbery as established fact. Its subhead described White as "Successfully Pursued" and the beating as "a Good Threshing," and the text called him "the culprit." Its opening line and its note on where White was caught tied the episode to George White's lynching.
No account by White himself appears, and no coverage of the episode was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Evening Journal Newport correspondent
accounts.gist: White robbed a State Road family that had sheltered him; the head of the family and his neighbors chased him to Newport and into the woods, recovered most of the property, gave him 'a heavy thrashing' and let him go. The robbery account is the accusers' version; White's own account does not appear.

framing.detail: The headline 'ROBBED PEOPLE WHO TOOK HIM IN' and the subhead's 'Successfully Pursued and a Good Threshing Administered' present the robbery as fact and the beating approvingly, calling White 'the culprit' and linking him to his lynched cousin.

A small armed pursuing party of private citizens (three seen), not a crowd

info: Tuesday, Aug. 11, 1903 ('yesterday' in a dispatch dated Aug. 12; White had been in New Castle on Monday and spent that night at State Road)
Pursuit began at State Road; chase through Newport, to a house in 'colored row', across Robert Lynam's field and the Snyder farm; capture in the woods near the spot of George White's alleged crime
Joseph White, described as a 'colored man' and a cousin of George White
Accused of taking $20, a gold watch, a revolver and a music box from a State Road family that had taken him in overnight and fed him
The head of the robbed family and the neighbors he roused; in Newport White was seen chased by 'three others' flourishing pistols and guns; race of pursuers not stated
White was released after the thrashing; the music box, which he had thrown away, was not reported recovered

sources.note: Special from Newport dated Aug. 12: Joseph White, 'colored man' and cousin of the lynched George White, accused of robbing a State Road family, chased through Newport, caught in the woods, thrashed and released.
quotes: Cousin of George White Successfully Pursued and a Good Threshing Administered.
This town was thrown into a state of excitement yesterday by the appearance of a colored man being chased by three others, the latter flourishing pistols and guns.
A heavy thrashing was administered to the culprit and he was released.
